pool.name: CS Fundamentals — Introduction to Computers
pool.description: 30 questions: 10 easy, 10 medium, 10 hard. Each randomized test draws 2 of each difficulty. Covers computer basics, history, types, applications, interfaces, and an ATM transaction.

notes.title: 1. What Is a Computer?
notes.summary: Meet a programmable machine and learn the input–processing–output–storage model using familiar examples.
notes.contentHtml:
Objective: feel comfortable with the idea of a computer

No coding experience is needed. By the end of this topic, you will be able to explain what a computer is and recognize different computers around you.

A simple definition

A computer is an electronic, programmable machine that accepts data, follows instructions to process it, and produces results. It can also store data and instructions for later use. Data means facts represented in a form a computer can use, such as numbers, words, pictures, or sensor readings.

Think of a helpful kitchen assistant: you give it ingredients and a recipe, it follows the steps, and it gives you a meal. A computer works with data and instructions rather than ingredients. Unlike a person, it does not need to understand your intention to carry out a program.

Four useful ideas: input, processing, output, storage

  • Input: data or instructions entering the system. Typing a number, tapping a button, or measuring temperature are inputs.
  • Processing: working on the input according to instructions. Adding prices or checking whether a PIN is valid are processing tasks.
  • Output: a result leaving the system, such as text on a screen, sound from a speaker, or a signal to a motor.
  • Storage: keeping data or programs so they can be used later, such as saving a photo or recording a transaction.

Example: in a calculator app, entering 7 + 5 is input; adding the numbers is processing; displaying 12 is output; saving the calculation in history is storage. Not every calculation needs to be saved.

This model describes roles, not four rigid steps that happen exactly once. A system may read stored data, process it, produce output, and store an updated result repeatedly.

What does programmable mean?

A program is a set of instructions. A programmable machine can carry out tasks according to programs, and its behavior can change when those instructions change. The same laptop can play music, edit a document, or calculate a budget by running different software. Some computers run a narrow, fixed set of programs; they are still computers.

Computers are not just boxes on desks

A phone, an ATM, a smart TV, a smartwatch, and the electronic controllers inside a modern car all use computers. A screen or keyboard is not required: a controller can get input from sensors and send output to a motor.

Quick check

A phone camera receives light through a sensor (input), prepares an image (processing), shows a preview (output), and saves the photo (storage). Can you describe another example in your own words?

notes.title: 2. Why Were Computers Invented?
notes.summary: Discover how counting aids and programmable electronic machines helped people handle calculation and repetitive work.
notes.contentHtml:
Why build a machine to work with information?

People can calculate, organize records, and repeat tasks, but large amounts of work take time. We get tired, lose track of steps, and make mistakes. Navigation, scientific experiments, business accounts, and population records created a need for faster and more dependable information processing.

A gradual evolution, not one single invention

  1. Counting aids: devices such as the abacus helped people keep track of calculations. An abacus is a human-operated aid, not a modern electronic computer.
  2. Mechanical calculators: gears and other moving parts performed arithmetic. These reduced manual calculation, although they were much less flexible than modern computers.
  3. Ideas for programmable machines: in the 1800s, Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, an important early concept for a general-purpose mechanical computer. It was not completed in his lifetime.
  4. Electronic computers: early electronic machines in the 1940s supported large calculations, including scientific and military work. Many were very large and needed specialist operators.
  5. Smaller components: transistors, integrated circuits, and microprocessors helped computers become smaller, more affordable, and practical for everyday products.

There is no need to memorize dates here. Notice the direction: from helping a person count to automatically following increasingly flexible programs.

What changed?

  • Communication: networked computers enabled email, messaging, and video calls over long distances.
  • Science: computers analyze measurements and simulate systems such as weather. A simulation is a model, not a guarantee that a prediction is correct.
  • Business: computers help manage payroll, stock, transactions, and customer records at large scale.

Fast does not mean infallible

Computers can repeat instructions quickly and consistently, but wrong input, incorrect programs, broken hardware, or unsuitable assumptions can produce wrong results. If a shop enters the wrong price, calculating it quickly will not fix the price.

Computers extend human capabilities. People still need to choose goals, check evidence, and judge whether a result makes sense.

notes.title: 3. Types of Computers
notes.summary: Compare personal devices, servers, supercomputers, and embedded systems without confusing size with purpose.
notes.contentHtml:
Different computers, different jobs

Computers vary in size, portability, power use, and purpose. A larger case does not automatically make a computer more useful for every task.

Personal computers and mobile devices

  • Desktop: usually stays at a desk, with a separate display and input devices. Useful for home, school, and office work.
  • Laptop: a portable computer with a built-in display, keyboard, and battery.
  • Smartphone: a pocket-sized computer with apps, wireless communication, sensors, and a touchscreen.
  • Tablet: a portable touchscreen computer, usually with a larger screen than a phone. It may also use a stylus or keyboard.

Computers behind the scenes

  • Server: a computer or software system providing data or services to other devices. A school server might store shared files; a web server responds to requests for pages. Server describes a role, not one required shape or size.
  • Supercomputer: a very high-performance computing system designed for demanding large-scale work, such as climate modeling or scientific simulations. It is not simply a desktop with a large monitor.
  • Embedded system: a computing system built into a larger product, often for a specific control or monitoring job. Examples include a washing-machine controller, a car's braking controller, and a temperature controller.

General-purpose versus special-purpose

A general-purpose computer can run many kinds of applications. A laptop can write essays, browse the web, and play music. A special-purpose computer is designed or configured for a narrower job, such as controlling a washing cycle or operating an ATM.

These are different ways to classify systems, not mutually exclusive lists. A server can use general-purpose hardware. An ATM may use general-purpose components but is deployed as a special-purpose system. A smartwatch can run multiple apps while also containing embedded controllers.

Try classifying these

A laptop in a library is a personal, usually general-purpose computer. A controller inside a lift is an embedded, special-purpose system. A machine providing the library's catalog to many users is acting as a server.

Ask two questions: what physical form does it have, and what job is it doing?

notes.title: 4. Where Are Computers Used?
notes.summary: Connect computer functions to education, healthcare, banking, transportation, entertainment, and industry.
notes.contentHtml:
Computers are part of everyday systems

Once you look for input, processing, output, and storage, computing becomes easier to recognize.

  • Education: learning platforms display lessons, collect quiz answers, calculate results, and store progress. A teacher still decides how best to support a learner.
  • Medicine: hospital systems store patient records, display scans, and help staff monitor readings. Medical professionals interpret results and make clinical decisions.
  • Banking: computers check transactions, update account records, and provide ATM and online-banking services. Accuracy, security, and privacy matter because these records affect real money.
  • Transportation: navigation apps use location and map data to suggest routes. Traffic controllers use sensors and rules to operate signals. Modern vehicles contain controllers for functions such as braking and engine management.
  • Entertainment: computers run games, edit video, stream music, and recommend content. A smart TV combines computing with a display and network connection.

Computers hidden in appliances

A modern automatic washing machine may receive the chosen cycle and water-level readings as input, decide how long to run each stage, control valves and motors as output, and keep settings in storage. The screen is only one possible output; moving a motor is another.

Not every electrical appliance is a computer. A simple electrical switch can turn a lamp on without executing a program. A device's computing behavior depends on the controller it contains, not simply on whether it uses electricity.

Industrial systems

A factory controller can read temperature sensors, compare measurements with a target, and adjust a heater. A warehouse system can track stock and help plan deliveries. These systems must be checked for faults, especially when a wrong output could harm people.

Useful limits

Automation can reduce repetitive work, but computers depend on suitable data, instructions, power, and maintenance. Some tasks work offline; tasks that need a remote service may require a network connection.

Observe your surroundings

Find three likely computers at home or school. For each, name a job it performs and at least one input and one output. Do not open appliances or interfere with safety equipment.

notes.title: 5. How Humans Interact with Computers
notes.summary: Understand input and output devices, touch and voice interfaces, and how hardware and software work together.
notes.contentHtml:
How do we give instructions and receive results?

An interface is a way to interact with a system. Buttons, screens, menus, sounds, and spoken commands can all be parts of an interface.

Input devices

A keyboard sends key presses, a mouse sends movements and clicks, a microphone captures sound, a camera captures images, and sensors measure things such as motion or temperature. These are ways for data to enter a computer.

Output devices

A monitor shows information, speakers produce sound, and a printer produces a paper copy. Outputs can also control the physical world: a controller may send a signal that operates a motor or warning light.

A touchscreen does two jobs

The display presents information as output. The touch-sensitive layer detects taps or gestures as input. One physical device can perform more than one role; classify what it is doing rather than forcing it into only one box.

Voice interfaces

When you ask a voice assistant to set a timer, the microphone captures speech (input), software interprets the request (processing), and the speaker or screen confirms it (output). Recognition can fail because of noise or unclear speech. Some voice features run on the device, while others need a remote service.

Hardware and software are complementary

Hardware is the physical equipment: processor, memory chips, keyboard, screen, and storage drive. Software is the programs and instructions that tell that equipment what to do, including operating systems and apps.

A piano and a music score are a useful analogy: the instrument is physical, and the score describes actions to perform. In a computer, hardware performs operations according to software. An app is not a physical part; a screen is not a program.

Hardware alone does not decide which app behavior you want. Software needs compatible hardware to execute. Changing software can change behavior without replacing the hardware, but some tasks also need specific physical equipment.

Interfaces should fit the learner

People may use keyboard navigation, screen readers, large text, touch, or voice. Offering multiple ways to interact can improve accessibility. Voice is not always suitable in a noisy or private setting.

notes.title: 6. Practical Activity — Follow an ATM Transaction
notes.summary: Identify input, processing, output, and storage in a safe, fictional withdrawal; finish with a self-check rubric.
notes.contentHtml:
Your mission

Explain how an ATM uses computing to help a customer withdraw money. Use this fictional example only: an account has 100 units and the customer requests 20 units. Do not use real card numbers, PINs, account details, or an actual ATM for this exercise.

First, try it yourself

  1. Draw four boxes labeled Input, Processing, Output, and Storage.
  2. Place these events in the appropriate boxes: read card information; enter a PIN; request 20 units; check the PIN and available balance; display approval or rejection; dispense cash after approval; record the completed withdrawal.
  3. Explain where the account balance is kept and why it needs to survive a restart.
  4. Explain why the machine must not dispense cash simply because someone typed an amount.

Worked walkthrough

  1. Input: the card reader receives card information, and the keypad or touchscreen receives the PIN and requested amount. Never write a real PIN in your answer.
  2. Processing: the ATM and bank systems check credentials, account funds, transaction limits, and availability. They decide whether the withdrawal can proceed. For this simplified successful example, the new balance is 100 − 20 = 80 units.
  3. Output: the screen shows a message, the dispenser releases approved cash, and a printer may produce a receipt. A declined transaction also has output, such as an explanation on the screen.
  4. Storage: bank systems durably record the completed transaction and updated account balance. The authoritative account record is normally held by the bank's systems, not only on the ATM screen or card.

This is a teaching model, not a complete banking protocol. Real systems handle fees, network failures, cash-dispenser faults, and reconciliation. They must keep records and cash outcomes consistent; a request alone is not proof that cash was dispensed.

Discuss two variations

Insufficient funds: if only 10 units are available and 20 are requested, the system should reject the withdrawal. A rejection message is output; it is not a successful debit. A failed attempt may still be logged.

Lost connection: the ATM may be unable to get approval. It should not assume a displayed balance or an unverified request is enough to safely complete a withdrawal.

Self-check

  • I can define a computer as a programmable machine that processes data.
  • I can name phones, laptops, servers, and embedded controllers as examples.
  • I can distinguish input, processing, output, and storage in the ATM example.
  • I can explain why a touchscreen can be both input and output.
  • I can explain that hardware is physical equipment and software supplies instructions.

Completion outcome

Explain what a computer is in two sentences, identify three different computers around you, and describe their inputs and outputs. Then take a six-question test: two easy, two medium, and two hard questions drawn from the 30-question pool. Hard questions require reasoning about these same beginner concepts, not knowledge of programming.

questions.questionText: Which description best explains what a computer is?
options: Only a screen used to watch videos
An electronic programmable machine that processes data
Any object that uses electricity
A machine that always understands human intentions
questions.explanation: A computer follows programs to process data. Electricity or a screen alone does not make a device a computer.

questions.questionText: Which action is input when using a calculator app?
options: Showing the answer
Adding two values internally
Typing the numbers
Saving a past calculation
questions.explanation: Typing sends data into the app. Displaying is output, adding is processing, and saving is storage.

questions.questionText: What is the computer doing when it adds the prices in a shopping basket?
options: Processing
Printing
Receiving keyboard input
Storing a receipt
questions.explanation: Calculating a total transforms input data according to instructions, so it is processing.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of output?
options: A microphone capturing speech
A sensor reading temperature
A keyboard detecting a key press
A speaker playing a notification
questions.explanation: The speaker sends a result out as sound. The other actions collect input.

questions.questionText: Why does a computer save a document to storage?
options: To turn the keyboard into software
To keep the document available for later use
To guarantee that its contents are correct
To stop all processing permanently
questions.explanation: Storage retains data for later use. Saving a document does not guarantee its accuracy.

questions.questionText: Which need helped motivate the development of computers?
options: Removing the need for all human decisions
Making every calculation slower
Handling large calculations and repetitive record work
Ensuring incorrect instructions always produce correct results
questions.explanation: Computers helped address the time, repetition, and error risks of large manual information-processing tasks.

questions.questionText: Which computer normally combines a built-in keyboard, display, and battery in a portable unit?
options: Laptop
Desktop monitor alone
Mechanical abacus
Printer
questions.explanation: A laptop integrates those components into a portable personal computer.

questions.questionText: What is the main role of a server?
options: To be carried on a wrist
To work only without software
To replace every input device
To provide data or services to other devices
questions.explanation: Server describes the role of providing resources or services, such as shared files or web pages.

questions.questionText: Which item is software?
options: A physical keyboard
A music-player application
A storage drive
A microphone
questions.explanation: An application is software: instructions executed by hardware. The other items are physical equipment.

questions.questionText: Which pair names everyday products that contain computers?
options: A paper notebook and a wooden ruler
A plain chair and a glass cup
A smartphone and a smartwatch
An unpowered pencil and a sheet of paper
questions.explanation: Smartphones and smartwatches contain processors that execute programs and work with data.

questions.questionText: A phone shows a button and detects your tap on it. Which roles does its touchscreen perform?
options: Output when displaying, and input when detecting the tap
Storage only, for both actions
Processing only, for both actions
Input when displaying, and output when detecting the tap
questions.explanation: The display presents output, while the touch-sensitive layer receives input. A physical device can have multiple roles.

questions.questionText: Why can one laptop edit a document and also play a game?
options: Its screen automatically invents all instructions
Its hardware must be replaced for every task
It has no need for programs
Different programs make the same general-purpose hardware perform different tasks
questions.explanation: Programmability allows general-purpose hardware to perform different tasks by executing different software.

questions.questionText: Which is the clearest example of an embedded, special-purpose computing system?
options: A laptop used for writing, games, and browsing
A controller built into a washing machine to manage wash cycles
A tablet running many unrelated apps
A desktop used for video editing and accounting
questions.explanation: The washing-machine controller is part of a larger product and focuses on controlling that product.

questions.questionText: A research team needs large-scale climate simulations. Which type of system is designed for this demanding computation?
options: An ordinary touchscreen with no processor
A mechanical counting frame
A supercomputer
A speaker used alone
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are designed for demanding large-scale computation such as climate modeling.

questions.questionText: A shop's program correctly adds item prices, but an employee entered one price incorrectly. Why can the total still be wrong?
options: Correct processing can produce an unsuitable result from incorrect input
Computers never process numbers
Fast processing guarantees correct input
The printer changes every entered price
questions.explanation: A program can follow its rules correctly while using incorrect data. Speed does not repair bad input.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the evolution from the abacus to modern computers?
options: The abacus was a battery-powered electronic computer
Every early calculating device could run modern apps
All modern computers were invented at one moment for one purpose
Human-operated calculating aids were followed by increasingly automated and programmable machines
questions.explanation: Computing developed gradually. An abacus helps a person calculate but is not a modern electronic programmable computer.

questions.questionText: You ask a voice assistant to set a timer. Which sequence correctly identifies input, processing, and output?
options: Speaker captures words; microphone interprets them; app becomes hardware
Microphone captures speech; software interprets the request; speaker confirms the timer
Stored timer is input; your voice is storage; interpretation is output
Screen stores your speech permanently; keyboard rings the alarm; software is unnecessary
questions.explanation: Speech is captured as input, interpreted through processing, and followed by a confirmation as output.

questions.questionText: In the simplified ATM activity, which action is processing rather than input, output, or storage?
options: The customer types a requested amount
The machine prints a receipt
The bank checks whether the available balance covers the request
The bank retains the completed transaction record
questions.explanation: Checking funds is a decision made by processing data. Typing is input, printing is output, and retaining records is storage.

questions.questionText: Which example correctly connects a field of use to a computing task?
options: Healthcare: storing patient records and displaying scans for professionals
Education: guaranteeing understanding without teaching or practice
Transportation: making sensors unnecessary in all vehicles
Banking: approving every withdrawal regardless of account funds
questions.explanation: Computers support healthcare records and imaging. They do not remove the need for professional judgment, valid data, or rules.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly relates hardware and software?
options: A keyboard is software because it sends instructions
Software can execute without any compatible physical computing system
Hardware and software are two names for the same thing
Hardware provides physical components; software provides instructions they execute
questions.explanation: Physical components and programs complement each other. Software requires compatible hardware to run.

questions.questionText: A classroom laptop is configured to provide shared files to other devices. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: It stops being a computer because laptops cannot share files
It is acting as a server even though its physical form is a laptop
It becomes a supercomputer because several people connect
It no longer needs software once files are saved
questions.explanation: Server describes a service-providing role, not a mandatory physical size or shape. A laptop can take that role.

questions.questionText: An ATM is built with hardware similar to a desktop, but customers can only perform banking operations. How should its deployed purpose be described?
options: It cannot be programmable because its interface is restricted
It must be general-purpose for customers because of its components
It is a special-purpose system, even if it uses general-purpose hardware internally
It is only an output device because it dispenses cash
questions.explanation: Purpose and underlying hardware are different classifications. A restricted banking system can use general-purpose components.

questions.questionText: In the activity, an account contains 100 units and a 20-unit withdrawal completes successfully with no fees. Which result correctly combines processing and storage?
options: Compute 80 units and durably record the updated balance and completed transaction
Compute 120 units and save only the customer's button press
Show 80 units but retain 100 as the authoritative balance forever
Delete the account record because the cash has left the machine
questions.explanation: Subtracting gives 80. Durable bank records must reflect the completed withdrawal; a screen message alone is not storage of the account update.

questions.questionText: An ATM rejects a request for 20 units because only 10 are available. Which statement is correct?
options: There is no output because no cash leaves the ATM
The PIN automatically becomes output
Every rejected request must be recorded as a completed withdrawal
The rejection message is output, and the attempt may be logged without a successful withdrawal debit
questions.explanation: Output includes messages, not just cash. A failed attempt may be logged, but rejection is not a completed cash withdrawal.

questions.questionText: A temperature controller has no screen or keyboard. It reads a sensor and operates a heater according to a program. Is it a computer-based system?
options: No, because every computer must have a keyboard
Yes: sensor readings are input, program decisions are processing, and heater-control signals are output
No, because only human-entered data can be input
Yes, but only while connected to the internet
questions.explanation: Embedded computing can use sensors and actuators instead of human-facing devices. A screen, keyboard, and internet access are not defining requirements.

questions.questionText: Which scenario best shows why a fast computer can still produce an unreliable conclusion?
options: A calculation takes less time than it would by hand
A screen displays the result clearly
A weather model runs quickly but uses incorrect measurements and unsuitable assumptions
A bank stores records durably after a verified transaction
questions.explanation: Speed does not establish data quality or model validity. Wrong measurements or assumptions can undermine a result.

questions.questionText: A phone captures a photo, displays it, and saves it. Later, the gallery reads the saved photo for display. What does this show about input, processing, output, and storage?
options: The roles can recur, and stored data can be read for later processing and output
The four roles must each happen exactly once and only in one fixed order
Once data is stored, it cannot become useful to processing again
Displaying a saved photo proves it was never stored
questions.explanation: The four-part model is not a rigid one-pass pipeline. Programs repeatedly read and use stored data to produce results.

questions.questionText: A car contains controllers for braking and engine management. Why is saying 'a computer is only a desktop or laptop' misleading?
options: Cars never contain software
Every part of a car is a general-purpose computer
A processor is useful only when a driver can type into it
Computers can be embedded inside larger products and perform specialized control tasks
questions.explanation: Embedded controllers execute programs within larger systems. Computing is not limited to standalone personal devices.

questions.questionText: An ATM loses its connection to the bank before approval. Which conclusion best follows from the activity's model?
options: The customer's typed amount alone proves the funds are available
It should not assume the withdrawal is safe simply because input was received; approval and consistent records still matter
A local screen automatically becomes the authoritative bank record
Loss of connection means every attempted withdrawal must be treated as completed
questions.explanation: Receiving a request is not the same as validating and completing it. Real systems must handle authorization, failures, and consistent transaction records.

questions.questionText: A plain switch turns a lamp on, while a programmable controller uses sensor readings to choose a lighting schedule. Which distinction is most useful?
options: Both must be computers because both use electricity
Neither can involve computing without a touchscreen
The controller follows a program to process data; using electricity alone does not establish that a device is a computer
The plain switch must store a general-purpose operating system
questions.explanation: Programmable data processing is the relevant distinction. A simple electrical circuit need not execute a program.
